title: France and England Meet in World Cup Third-Place Playoff With Golden Boot and Legacy on the Line
excerpt: Kylian Mbappé chases a second consecutive Golden Boot while Didier Deschamps takes charge of his final match as France manager in Saturday's bronze medal game at Hard Rock Stadium.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • France and England meet for the World Cup third-place playoff at Hard Rock Stadium.
  • Kylian Mbappé leads the Golden Boot race with eight goals, tied with Lionel Messi.
  • Didier Deschamps manages his final match for France after 14 years.
  • Both teams will make significant lineup changes after semifinal losses.
  • France faces England at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami on Saturday at 5 p.m. ET for the World Cup third-place playoff
  • Kylian Mbappé leads the Golden Boot race with eight goals, tied with Lionel Messi, while Harry Kane trails by two
  • Didier Deschamps takes charge of his 187th and final match as France manager after 14 years at the helm
  • Both sides are expected to make significant lineup changes after semifinal heartbreak earlier in the week

A Consolation Prize Neither Side Wanted

Neither France nor England envisioned ending their World Cup campaigns this way. Both arrived in the United States as genuine title contenders, and both were eliminated in agonizing fashion in Wednesday's semifinals. France, many bookmakers' pre-tournament favorite, was shut out by a ruthless Spain side. England's exit was even more painful — leading Argentina 1-0 in the 85th minute before conceding twice in seven minutes to lose 2-1 in regulation.

Now, instead of preparing for Sunday's final, they meet at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens for a game that sits somewhere between a glorified friendly and a meaningful international fixture. The match kicks off at 5 p.m. ET on Saturday, airing on Fox and Telemundo in the United States.

Mbappé's Golden Boot Chase

"Kylian Mbappé sits on eight goals for the tournament, level with Lionel Messi at the top of the scoring charts."

"ET on Saturday, airing on Fox and Telemundo in the United States.</p> <h2>Mbappé's Golden Boot Chase</h2> <p>Whatever the match lacks in title stakes, it makes up for in individual storylines."

Whatever the match lacks in title stakes, it makes up for in individual storylines. Kylian Mbappé sits on eight goals for the tournament, level with Lionel Messi at the top of the scoring charts. A goal or two on Saturday could hand the 27-year-old a second consecutive Golden Boot — a feat that would further cement his status among the greatest World Cup performers in history.

"Mbappé will be particularly motivated as he chases a second successive World Cup Golden Boot."

— Sports Illustrated

France have been relentlessly lethal throughout the tournament, leading all teams in expected goals (14.6), shots on target per match (7.1), and big chances created (27). Michael Olise has been the tournament's leading assist provider with five. The firepower is there for a statement performance.

Harry Kane, trailing Mbappé by two goals, has an outside chance at the Golden Boot himself. The Bayern Munich striker will lead the line once more as he looks to end what may be his last World Cup on a personal high.

Deschamps' Farewell and England's Rotation

Saturday marks the end of an era for French football. Didier Deschamps, who has managed Les Bleus since 2012 across 187 matches, will take charge for the final time. Under his stewardship, France won the 2018 World Cup and reached the 2022 final. His players will want to send him off with a victory.

Both managers are expected to rotate heavily. France will be without center back William Saliba, who suffered a back injury against Spain. Crystal Palace's Maxence Lacroix will likely slot in alongside Ibrahima Konaté. Brice Samba may start in goal, and midfield options Manu Koné and Warren Zaïre-Emery could get the nod.

Thomas Tuchel's England will look significantly different as well. Jordan Henderson is out with a broken wrist. Declan Rice, battling fitness issues throughout the tournament, will rest. Kobbie Mainoo, who has not played a minute at this World Cup, is likely to earn his first start alongside Reece James in midfield. Marcus Rashford, Ollie Watkins, and Eberechi Eze could all feature from the start.

World Cup playoff history

France has won two of its three previous third-place playoffs, triumphing in 1958 and 1986. England has lost both of its previous bronze medal matches, finishing fourth in 1990 and 2018. The head-to-head record between the nations across 32 previous meetings gives England the edge overall — 17 wins to France's 10 — but Les Bleus won their most recent encounter, a 2-1 victory in the 2022 World Cup quarterfinal when Kane missed a crucial late penalty.

For Indian diaspora fans in the United States, the match offers prime-time Saturday viewing as the tournament's penultimate game before Sunday's Argentina-Spain final. With the match falling outside traditional work hours, it is one fixture that employers, at least, will not need to worry about.
